$ SHORT PER $1 LONG: Minimum-variance hedge ratio. 1.06 = short $1.06 of this for every $1 of the long.
% OF VARIANCE: How much of the stock's total price risk this factor accounts for.
13F AS OF: Latest 13F quarter loaded. Filings arrive about 45 days after quarter end, so this engine always lags.
13F FUND FLOW (bps): Net change in the share of the company held by your watchlist funds last quarter, in basis points of shares outstanding.
2-YEAR RANGE: Lowest and highest rolling empirical ratio over two years.
ADDS RISK: Total variance goes up with this hedge on.
AFTER: Net loading of long minus hedge. Anything still large (orange label) is a bet you are still making.
ANALYST REVISIONS vs PEERS (σ): Engine 1 score: how strongly analysts are raising (+) or cutting (−) this stock, in standard deviations against its own subsector.
ANNUALIZED VOLATILITY: Standard deviation of returns, annualized, from 2 years of weekly data.
AVERAGE DAILY $ VOLUME (M): Average dollars traded per day, in millions.
BASKET SETTINGS: How many names the optimized basket may hold, and the maximum weight of any one.
BASKET WEIGHTING: EQUAL = every stock counts the same (matches the small/mid-cap focus). CAP = weighted by market value.
BETA SHRINKAGE: Small-cap betas are noisy, so each loading is pulled 30% of the way toward its subsector average before use.
BORROW: EASY / HARD to borrow for shorting, proxied from size, short interest and liquidity.
BUSINESS INFLECTION DECILE: Engine 2 rank within the universe. D10 = strongest improving fundamentals, D1 = weakest.
CANDIDATE POOL: Where hedge candidates are drawn from.
CHANGE IN E1 GAP, 4 WEEKS: How much the average analyst-revision score gap between the long and short side widened in four weeks, in σ.
CHANGE OVER 4 WEEKS (pp): How much the revision-breadth gap widened (+) or narrowed (−) in the last four weeks. The list is sorted on this, because what just changed is the point, not what has been true for months.
CONFIDENCE BAND: ±1 standard error around the mean. Where the band includes zero, the result is not distinguishable from noise at that horizon.
CONTAINS TARGET: This ETF holds the stock you are long, so part of the short cancels your own position.
CONTROL GROUP: The same pairs in weeks when no flag fired. Without this, any positive result could just be the drift of the pair universe rather than the signal.
CORRELATION, LONG vs HEDGE: Correlation of weekly returns over two years.
CROWDED: Held by an unusually high share of your watchlist funds. Kept, but a late-trade warning.
CROWDED LONG: More than 60% of your watchlist funds already hold the long leg.
CROWDING: How widely owned each leg is among your watchlist funds. A heavily owned long leg is a late, crowded trade.
DAYS TO NEXT EARNINGS: Calendar days until the hedge's next earnings report, a scheduled risk for any short.
DECAY CURVE: Cumulative mean forward relative return, week by week after the event. The shape tells you the horizon: where it stops rising is where the edge is exhausted, and that sets the rebalance cadence.
EARNINGS INSIDE 30 DAYS: How many basket names report within 30 days.
EMPIRICAL CROSS-CHECK: The same hedge measured from raw return history instead of the factor model. When model and history disagree, trust neither.
EMPIRICAL NOW: Hedge ratio from the latest 52 weeks of raw returns.
ENGINE 1 · ANALYST REVISIONS: Are analysts raising or cutting price targets and estimates? Measured here as breadth: the share of names in a group being raised minus the share being cut. A leading signal, weekly.
ENGINE 2 · BUSINESS INFLECTION: Is the business itself improving (margins, growth, returns, leverage), from the financial statements? Measured as breadth: share of names inflecting up minus share deteriorating. A leading signal, weekly.
ENGINE 3 · 13F FUND FLOWS: What your watchlist of respected funds did last quarter. A lagging, confirming signal: it arrives about 45 days after quarter end.
ENGINE 4 · FACTOR MODEL: Your 14-factor regression applied to the spread (long minus short). It answers: is this pair a real stock-specific bet, or a disguised bet on momentum, rates, oil, etc.?
ENGINES DISAGREE: Analyst revisions favour the long leg but business fundamentals favour the short leg (or vice versa). Find out which is right before doing anything.
EQUAL-WEIGHT − CAP-WEIGHT RETURN, 1M: The pair's 1-month return using equal-weighted baskets minus the same using market-cap-weighted baskets. A large gap means a few mega-caps drive the cap-weighted picture and the typical stock is telling a different story.
EVENTS: Number of pair-weeks in the slice. Below ~200 nothing here should be trusted.
FACTOR: One of the 14 systematic return drivers in your Engine 4 model. Names here are placeholders for your actual set.
FACTOR BET: Less than 40% of the spread's risk is stock-specific. You would mostly be trading the factor named in the 'largest net factor' column.
FACTOR RISK REMOVED: Percent of the long's factor-driven variance that the hedge cancels.
FACTOR RISK REMOVED (%): Percent of the long's factor-driven variance this hedge cancels.
FACTOR SHARE: Percent of the stock's risk explained by the 14 factors. This is the part a hedge can remove.
FACTORS AS OF: Date of the latest 14-factor model run (Engine 4).
FAILS SIGNAL GATE: Analysts are raising and fundamentals are strong. Shown for context, excluded from selection.
FIRED SIDE · E1 (σ): Analyst-revision score of the company whose signal moved first.
FLAGS: Rule-based labels. Hover each one for its definition.
FORWARD RELATIVE RETURN: Long-leg return minus short-leg return over the window AFTER the event, measured from the week the flag fired. This is what the tab is claiming it can predict.
FROM: Where the idea came from in the platform.
FUNDAMENTALS AS OF: Date of the latest Engine 2 (business inflection) run.
FUNDS HOLDING, LONG / SHORT: Percent of your watchlist funds that hold names in each leg. A high first number = crowded long. A high second number = smart money still owns what you would be shorting.
GROSS SHORT: Total dollars shorted across the basket for the chosen notional.
HEDGE: The candidate: a single stock, an ETF, or an optimized basket.
HEDGE EFFICIENCY (0 to 1): How much of the two legs' price risk cancels when you hold one against the other: 1 − Var(long − short) ÷ (Var(long) + Var(short)), from 2 years of weekly returns. Near 1 = the legs move together, so the spread isolates their difference. Below 0.30 = not really a pair, just two separate bets; those rows are dimmed.
HEDGE RATIO: Dollars to short per $1 long so that variance is minimized.
HEDGE RATIO, FIRST YEAR / SECOND YEAR: The hedge ratio estimated separately on each half of the 2-year window. Far apart (red) = the relationship is unstable.
HEDGE RATIO, ROLLING 52 WEEKS: The empirical hedge ratio through time. Flat = dependable. Wandering = do not trust the number.
HEDGE'S 13F FUND FLOW (bps): Net change in your watchlist funds' ownership last quarter, in basis points of shares outstanding. Negative = funds are selling, which supports a short.
HEDGE'S ANALYST REVISIONS vs PEERS (σ): Engine 1 score of the hedge itself. For a short you want this negative (shown red = weak = better short). ETFs sit near zero.
HEDGE'S BUSINESS INFLECTION DECILE: Engine 2 rank of the hedge. D1 = weakest fundamentals (better short), D10 = strongest (do not short).
HIT RATE: Share of events where the forward relative return was positive. 50% is a coin flip. A modest edge with a high hit rate is more useful than a big edge driven by a few outliers.
INFLECTING: Engine 2 flags a fresh fundamental inflection.
INFLECTION BREADTH, LONG − SHORT (pp): Same idea as the revision column, but from financial statements: % of names in the long leg whose fundamentals are inflecting up minus the same for the short leg.
INFORMATION COEFFICIENT: Rank correlation between the size of the unpriced gap and the subsequent relative return, across all events. Answers whether a BIGGER gap led to a bigger move, not just whether the direction was right.
JOINED: Pairs that entered the top 10% by signal divergence this week.
LARGEST NET FACTOR EXPOSURE: The factor the spread is most exposed to after the legs partly cancel, with its net loading. 'MOM +0.62' = being long this pair is substantially a bet that momentum keeps working.
LEFT: Pairs that dropped out of the top 10% this week, because the gap narrowed or price caught up.
LINK: Two companies with a hand-curated economic relationship. → points from supplier to customer; ↔ marks substitutes or a shared input cost.
LOADING (β): Sensitivity of the stock to the factor. +1.18 on MKT = the stock tends to move 1.18% when the market factor moves 1%.
LONG / SHORT: L = the leg you would own, S = the leg you would sell against it. n = number of stocks in that basket. Baskets are equal-weighted with a liquidity floor.
LOW HEDGE EFFICIENCY: Hedge efficiency below 0.30: the legs do not move together, so this is two separate bets, not a pair.
MAXIMUM DRAWDOWN: Worst peak-to-trough loss of the hedged position over two years. How much pain to expect even if the thesis is right.
MAXIMUM SHORT INTEREST: Candidates with more than this percent of float already sold short are excluded (squeeze risk, expensive borrow).
MINIMUM AVERAGE DAILY VOLUME: Candidates trading less than this per day (in dollars) are excluded as too illiquid to short.
MODE: NEUTRALIZE = remove every exposure you have no view on (usually an ETF or basket). EXPRESS = short the weakest competitor so the short is a second source of return. BOTH = show all on one map.
MODE FIT: Which job this hedge suits. NEUTRALIZE removes risk. EXPRESS adds a second thesis leg. BOTH does some of each.
MODEL-IMPLIED RATIO: Hedge ratio from the factor model (dashed orange line).
NARROWING: The signal gap is still positive but shrank over the last 4 weeks.
NET FUND BUYERS, LONG − SHORT: From the latest 13F filings of your watchlist funds: (funds that added − funds that cut) in the long leg, minus the same count for the short leg. +7 = seven more net buyers on the long side. Lagging, quarterly.
NET LOADING BEFORE / AFTER: Grey bar = the long's exposure on its own. Orange bar = what remains once the selected hedge is on. Orange near zero = that exposure is cancelled.
NEW: Entered the widest-divergence decile this week.
NO ALPHA: An ETF carries no view: it removes risk but the short leg is not expected to fall on its own.
NOTIONAL: Dollar size of the long. Hedge sizes are quoted per $1 of this.
OFFSETS MOST: The two factor exposures of the long that this name does the most to cancel.
ON FRONTIER: No other candidate both removes more risk and has weaker signals. One of the efficient choices.
OTHER SIDE · E1 (σ): Analyst-revision score of the linked company. Near zero = analysts have not reacted there yet: the read-through.
OUT OF SAMPLE: Held-back period that no threshold was tuned on. Everything above is in-sample and will look better than reality.
OUTCOME DISTRIBUTION: The full spread of forward returns, not just the average. A mean driven by a fat right tail is a different product from a mean driven by a consistent shift — the first needs many positions to realise, the second does not.
PAIR UNIVERSE: How many Tier-1 basket pairs were built, from how many stocks.
PASS HEDGE EFFICIENCY: Pairs whose legs move together enough (efficiency ≥ 0.30) to count as real pairs. Only these are ranked.
PRICE RATIO: How the long leg's share price has performed against the short leg's. This is the 'share price performance' view of the pair.
PRICE RATIO vs OWN HISTORY (z): Where today's long÷short price ratio sits against its own 5-year average, in standard deviations. Above +2 = the spread is already stretched; only acceptable if the signals justify it.
PRICE RATIO, 13 WEEKS: Long-leg price index divided by short-leg price index, weekly for 13 weeks. Flat while the signal chart climbs = not priced yet.
PRICED: The price ratio has already moved with the signals (3-month relative return above +15% or price-ratio z above +1.5). Probably late.
RANK: Position in the list under the current sort (the orange column header).
READ: Plain-English flags that summarize the row. Hover any flag for its rule.
REALIZED R²: How much of the long's weekly return variation the hedge explained over the last 2 years.
REALIZED β TO THE LONG: From a plain regression of the long's weekly returns on the hedge's over 2 years. Should be close to the model's hedge ratio.
RESIDUAL SHARE: Percent of risk that is stock-specific. This is the part your thesis is about, and the part a hedge should leave alone.
RESIDUAL SHARE BEFORE → AFTER: Share of the position's risk that is stock-specific. Higher after = the position is now mostly about your thesis.
REVISION BREADTH, LONG − SHORT (pp): Breadth = % of names in a leg with net analyst target raises minus % with net cuts. This column is long-leg breadth minus short-leg breadth, in percentage points. +48 means analysts are far more positive on the long leg. The bar shows the same number.
REVISIONS AS OF: Date of the latest Engine 1 (analyst revisions) run.
RISK · FROM ENGINE 4: Computed from your 14-factor model: how much of the long's risk each hedge removes.
SAMPLE COVERAGE: What history actually exists per engine, and therefore how much of this page is evidence versus placeholder.
SAMPLE SPAN: How far back this slice's data reaches. Engine 1 Leg A accrues forward from go-live and cannot be backfilled, so it has the shortest span and the weakest evidence.
SCOPE: WITHIN SECTOR = only pair subsectors from the same sector. ALL = also allow cross-sector pairs.
SECTOR: The sector both legs belong to. 'A × B' means the legs sit in different sectors, which usually makes for a worse pair.
SELECTED: The hedge currently shown in the Before / After panel and the charts below.
SHORT INTEREST TOO HIGH: More than 15% of float is already sold short: squeeze risk. Removed from the short side.
SHORT INTEREST, % OF FLOAT: Shares sold short as a percent of tradable shares. Above ~15% = crowded short with squeeze risk.
SHORT LEG STILL OWNED: More than 40% of your watchlist funds hold the short leg. They may know something, or may be about to sell.
SHORTABILITY: Can you actually short it, and is anything scheduled?
SIGNAL GAP, 13 WEEKS: The revision-breadth gap (long − short) plotted weekly for 13 weeks. Steady climb = durable divergence; a single jump = one-week spike.
SIGNAL GATE: A single stock only qualifies as a short if it is in the bottom third of its peers on analyst revisions or business inflection, and your funds are not accumulating it. Signals filter the pool; they are never blended into the risk math.
SLICING THE SAMPLE: Each row re-runs the same test on a subset. Slices are for diagnosing WHERE the effect lives, not for picking the best one — with this many cuts, the best-looking row is partly luck. Treat a slice as real only if it is large, has a plausible mechanism, and survives out-of-sample.
SPREAD AFTER KILLS: How many names survive on each side once kill screens are applied.
SPREAD VOLATILITY: Annualized volatility of long minus hedge.
STABILITY OVER TIME: The same test run year by year. An edge that only worked in one regime is a regime bet. Watch for the result concentrating in a single year.
STATUS: Kill-screen results. TRAP = value-trap flag on a long. SI HIGH / M&A TALK = unsafe short. Killed names are excluded from the spread.
STOCK-SPECIFIC CORRELATION: Correlation between the long's and the hedge's returns after removing all 14 factors. High = they share an industry driver the model misses, which the hedge also cancels.
STOCK-SPECIFIC SHARE OF SPREAD RISK: Percent of the spread's variance NOT explained by your 14 factors. High = the pair isolates something company- or industry-specific. Low (red) = the pair is mostly a factor bet in disguise.
T-STATISTIC: How many standard errors the mean forward return sits above zero, clustered by week so that overlapping events in the same market conditions are not counted as independent. Below ~2 the result is not distinguishable from noise.
TAKEOVER RISK: Reported deal interest. A bid would spike the stock, so it is removed from the short side.
TARGET LONG: The stock you want to own and hedge.
THE HEDGE'S OWN SIGNALS: What Engines 1–3 say about the hedge itself. Used only as a gate (is this a sensible short?), never blended into the risk numbers.
THE PAIR: Two groups of stocks: a LONG leg you would own and a SHORT leg you would sell against it. Each pair is oriented so the long leg is the one with the stronger analyst revisions.
TICKER: Stock symbol. Struck-through rows were removed by a kill screen and are not in the pair.
TIER: T1 = basket of one subsector vs basket of another. T2 = best vs worst stocks inside one subsector. T3 = hand-curated linked companies (supplier/customer, substitutes).
TOTAL VARIANCE REMOVED: Percent of ALL the long's variance removed, after adding the hedge's own stock-specific noise. This is the honest number: a single-name hedge can cancel factors yet barely reduce total risk.
TOTAL VARIANCE REMOVED (%): Percent of the long's total variance removed, net of the noise the hedge itself adds. Negative = the hedge adds risk. The table is sorted on this.
TRAJECTORY · LAST 13 WEEKS: Two small charts side by side. If the left one (signals) has moved and the right one (prices) has not, the divergence is not priced yet.
TYPE: NAME = single stock. ETF = sector or industry fund. BASKET = several shorts weighted by the optimizer.
UNPRICED: Signal gap widened more than 8pp in 4 weeks while the long-vs-short return stayed inside ±3%. The research candidates.
UNPRICED GAP (σ): How far the signal gap has moved beyond what the price ratio has already moved, in standard deviations of this pair's own history. High positive = signals diverged and price has not followed. This is the number the tab exists to find.
UNSTABLE RATIO: First-year and second-year hedge ratios differ by more than 0.2.
VALUATION: Is the long leg already expensive against the short leg, compared with this pair's own history?
VALUATION RATIO vs OWN 5 YEARS: Long-leg median forward multiple divided by short-leg's, shown as a percentile of that ratio's own 5-year history. P90+ (red zone) = the long leg is already unusually expensive against the short leg. P10− (green zone) = unusually cheap.
VALUE TRAP: Engine 2 quality screen: cheap for a reason (accruals, deteriorating cash conversion). Removed from the long side.
VERDICT: STABLE if the rolling ratio stayed within ±0.15 of the model and the two half-window estimates agree.
VOLATILITY AFTER: Annualized volatility of long-minus-hedge. The unhedged long is 31.4%.
VOLATILITY BEFORE → AFTER: Annualized volatility of the long alone, then of the long-minus-hedge position.
WEEKS SINCE: Weeks since the first side's signal fired.
WEIGHT: Share of the short basket in this name. Capped at 25%.
WEIGHTED ANALYST REVISIONS: Basket-weighted average of the constituents' Engine 1 scores (same signal, averaged; not a blend of different signals).
WEIGHTED SHORT INTEREST: Basket-weighted average short interest, % of float.
WHAT COUNTS AS AN EVENT: A pair-week where the signal gap widened by more than 8pp over four weeks while the long-vs-short return stayed inside ±3% — i.e. the UNPRICED flag fired. Every such week in the sample is one observation.
WORST MONTH: Worst rolling 1-month return of the hedged position.
β: The numeric loading shown in the bar.
